title: Lend a session scope over the plane bus and bound IPC waits by deadline_ms
goal: Vision: V-10. Prerequisite for moving pillar implementations out of core (Mandate 84, rule 5). (1) Under a session ToolScope, plane_bus req sends gawd./gemi./tools./agents. topics only to the in-process prefix handler, so an implementation another process serves on the bus is unreachable from a scoped session. Lend the scope instead of forcing in-process: serve a one-off topic scope.<nonce> that answers {name,args} through ToolScope::call, name it in the payload as scope_topic, close it when the request returns, and route remotely when another process serves the topic. The lent topic carries no credential; it only reaches tools the scope already holds. (2) plane_bus_ipc post sets no read timeout, so a hung peer hangs the caller: honour a payload deadline_ms (milliseconds the caller waits from sending) as the read timeout, answer 'plane bus: deadline exceeded' on expiry, and keep the route, since a slow peer is not a dead one. The plug-host side of both already speaks this contract.

reuse.searched: core plane_bus req/req_watched/with_watched (the progress and cancel streams this extends), scoped_tools ToolScope::call (the authority the lent topic answers through), plane_bus_ipc post/remote/prune_stale_route_file (where the deadline and the slow-versus-dead distinction go).

limitations: Changes the rule that scoped tools never cross IPC: the lent topic sits behind the bus secret like every bus topic, and reaches only the tools the scope already holds, for as long as the request runs. Windows x86_64 first; Linux run before any pillar deletion that relies on it. Core's GEMI stream facade drains chunks only after the request returns, so streamed text is buffered either way; live delivery is out of scope here.
progress: Not started. The plug-host side is proven against core's wire format.
